title: Virna squash (Virna F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Virna squash is an F1 hybrid squash variety from Ramgo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Virna squash is an F1 hybrid squash variety, also sold or known as Virna F1. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Virna squash is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Virna F1, this is the same squash. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [squash variety finder](/crop-varieties/squash), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit squash fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** Harvest 70 to 80 days after transplanting.
**Yield:** 25 to 30 t/ha potential (company figure), 2 to 3 fruits per plant.
**Fruit:** Uniform fruits of 2 to 3 kg with orange flesh that is sweet and sticky.
Tolerant to fusarium wilt and virus.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: in Ramgo's professional squash line, only evidence is Ramgo's own listing. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual squash on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Virna squash

Choose a fruit size your buyer wants, from small round ones for households to big flat ones for the market. A thick, deep orange flesh keeps longer and sells better. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Virna F1 the same as Virna?
items.a: Yes. Virna F1 is another name for Virna. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Virna?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
